gaps.topic: TSMC fab-level EUV use (Fab 15, Fab 18, Fab 20, Fab 22, Arizona Fab 21)
gaps.why: TSMC's FY2025 annual report and 20-F mention EUV scanners only at company level and do not tie EUV to a fab. tsmc.com, esg.tsmc.com, pr.tsmc.com and investor.tsmc.com returned Cloudflare challenges or HTTP 403 to the declared project user agent, and sec.gov archive documents (including 2024 TSMC 6-Ks that EDGAR full-text search shows mention EUV) were refused as an undeclared tool. A TSMC ESG article (esg.tsmc.com/en-US/articles/371) is reported to name Fab 15B, Fab 18A and Fab 18B as EUV sites, but it could not be fetched to verify quotes.
gaps.would_need: A fetchable TSMC document tying EUV to specific fabs, such as esg.tsmc.com/en-US/articles/371, the TSMC sustainability report, tsmc.com logic technology pages (e.g. 'Fab 18 is the main 3nm production facility' plus an N3/N5 EUV statement), or a TSMC 6-K. Combined with ASML's 20-F sole-maker statement this would support req:tsmc-fab18-euv and others.

gaps.why: The CHIPS award page and Samsung documents reviewed describe Taylor as a leading-edge (2nm) logic fab but do not mention EUV lithography.
gaps.would_need: A Samsung release or filing stating that the Taylor fab uses EUV lithography.

gaps.topic: Micron Taiwan (Taichung/Taoyuan), Boise ID1 and Clay NY EUV requirement
gaps.why: Micron's FY2025 10-K ties EUV only to Hiroshima. Search results indicate Micron said it would ramp 1-gamma EUV in Taiwan and Japan (FY2024 10-K / earnings materials), but sec.gov archives and investors.micron.com refused the declared user agent, so the quote could not be verified.
gaps.would_need: A fetchable Micron 10-K/10-Q or release stating EUV production in Taiwan or at a named US fab.

gaps.topic: SK hynix Yongin cluster EUV requirement
gaps.why: SK hynix's 2026 424B4 allocates offering proceeds to EUV scanners and to construction of Korean production facilities but does not tie the EUV scanners to Yongin.
gaps.would_need: An SK hynix document stating that the Yongin fab will incorporate EUV lithography.

gaps.topic: TRUMPF as sole supplier of EUV drive lasers to ASML
gaps.why: TRUMPF's 2025 release calls the TRUMPF-ASML relationship a 'close and exclusive partnership', and ASML's FY2025 20-F does not name TRUMPF. No reviewed document uses 'sole' or 'single supplier' for the drive laser, so no single-supplier requirement was created. No document names the ASML site (e.g. San Diego light-source operations) that receives the lasers, so flow:trumpf-to-asml was not refined.
gaps.would_need: An ASML or TRUMPF filing or release stating that TRUMPF is the sole/single supplier of EUV CO2 drive lasers, and naming the receiving ASML site.

gaps.topic: ASML ship-from site for EUV systems (flow:asml-to-intel, -oregon, -arizona, -ireland)
gaps.why: ASML's 20-F lists final assembly across nine sites (Veldhoven, Eindhoven, Oirschot, Berlin, Wilton, San Diego, Pyeongtaek, Linkou, Tainan) without saying which site ships EUV systems. The Veldhoven page says the M&P department 'assembles, builds and delivers all our systems' but does not explicitly say EUV systems ship from Veldhoven. Because ASML's HQ is also Veldhoven, a refinement would not move the drawn route.
gaps.would_need: An ASML filing or release stating that EUV (NXE/EXE) systems undergo final assembly and shipment from Veldhoven.

gaps.topic: Wacker polysilicon routes (to Siltronic, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, SK siltron): source site
gaps.why: Siltronic's 2025 annual report says most of its polysilicon comes from Wacker under long-term agreements, but also says 'several production facilities of Wacker Chemie AG and other suppliers were qualified', so no single Wacker site can be pinned. Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers and SK siltron documents reviewed do not name Wacker or a Wacker site.
gaps.would_need: A Wacker or wafer-maker document naming the Wacker plant (Burghausen, Nünchritz or Charleston) that supplies a given wafer maker or site.

gaps.topic: Siltronic wafer routes (to Samsung, to Intel Arizona): source site and Samsung destination
gaps.why: Siltronic's annual report does not name customers or tie customer supply to its Singapore, Freiberg or Burghausen fabs.
gaps.would_need: A Siltronic or customer document naming the Siltronic fab and the receiving customer fab.

gaps.topic: Equipment and materials routes to TSMC/Samsung (Lam Research, Applied Materials, KLA, JSR, Shin-Etsu) and Ichor routes
gaps.why: The 10-Ks of Lam, Applied Materials, KLA and Ichor, and the JSR/Shin-Etsu releases reviewed, name customers at company level (e.g. >10% customers) but never tie a shipping plant to a customer fab.
gaps.would_need: A supplier release, CHIPS award or customer document naming the supplier plant and the receiving fab (e.g. a tool delivery to TSMC Arizona or an on-site materials plant).
